name: OP285 (ADI dual 9 MHz precision 'Butler' bipolar/JFET audio op-amp)
tagline: The laser-trimmed precision sibling of the OP275 (same Butler bipolar/JFET input, 9 MHz, 22 V/us). CN upgrade guides and Head-Fi users praise its sweet, resolving midrange.
technology: Dual voltage-feedback op-amp with ADI's 'Butler Amplifier' input stage, which pairs bipolar transistors (for accuracy and low noise) with JFETs (for speed). Its headline specs (9 MHz GBW, 22 V/us, 6 nV/rtHz, 0.0006% THD, 5 mA) match the OP275's. What sets it apart is a laser-trimmed input offset guaranteed below 250 uV. It is not faster than the OP275. Whether the two share a die is unconfirmed.

reputation.summary: A long-standing Chinese upgrade favourite that is almost always mentioned with the OP275. Reprinted CN op-amp guides (CSDN, ZOL, PCPOP, 21ic) credit OP275/OP285 with a soft, 'tube-like' midrange, intimate vocals and high resolution. One CN comparison says the OP285G sounds like the OP275G but with more colour saturation and a wider soundstage, and slightly less bass. Car-audio shops (sounting.com) list it as a 'fever-grade' op-amp. Head-Fi's 'I like the OP285' thread reports good resolution, a refined but resolving treble, and a sound that is 'right' overall, but posters say it needs care in the circuit. diyAudio's best-sounding-dual thread suggests it as a budget alternative to try alongside the OPA627/OPA637. All of this is enthusiast opinion, not measurement.
sonic_descriptors: more colour saturation and wider soundstage than OP275 (one CN comparison)
slightly less bass than OP275 (one CN comparison)

caveats: The praise mostly comes from reprinted CN guides and forum anecdotes, not measured comparisons.
Head-Fi posters say it needs careful circuit conditions (decoupling, loading) to sound its best.
The DIP-8 OP285GP was reportedly obsolete by about 2002. Socketed rolling today usually means SOIC OP285GSZ on an adapter, old stock or remarked parts.
Its headline specs are the same as the OP275's. Claims that it is 'faster' than the OP275 are wrong.

silicon_changes.identification: Non-Z SOIC part numbers are discontinued. The replacement carries the Z suffix: OP285GSZ (and its -REEL/-REEL7 versions).
silicon_changes.summary: Product discontinuance of the non-RoHS OP285GS variants, with OP285GSZ named as the pin-compatible replacement. The sources found document no die change. This is a part-number/lead-finish transition, not a case of the same part number with different silicon.

counterfeit_notes: No ADI counterfeit advisory was found. Marketplace listings (e.g. Amazon '5PCS OP285G OP285 OP285GS OP285GSZ OP285GSZ-REEL SOP8') lump several part numbers into one product, which is a common sign of remarked or mixed stock. The DIP-8 OP285GP is reportedly obsolete since about 2002, so fresh-looking DIP 'OP285GP' parts sold for op-amp rolling are likely old stock or remarked. Buy OP285GSZ through authorized distributors such as Arrow.
alternatives: OP275 (same Butler front end and headline specs, 1 mV offset grade, audio-marketed sibling)

refuted_claims: The draft called the OP285 the 'faster sibling of the OP275 (about 9 MHz GBW)'. This is refuted: the OP285's 9 MHz / 22 V/us match the OP275's (the OP275 is also listed as 9 MHz, e.g. https://uk.rs-online.com/web/p/op-amps/1832628). The OP285's distinction is its trimmed 250 uV max offset.
